enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
539 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 529 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

 - Isolated showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and evening, 
   limited to Southwest New Mexico.

 - Warm temperatures over the next couple days, with lowland highs 
   in the 80s. This is slightly above normal for late October.

 - Widespread chances for showers and thunderstorms return
   Thursday night through Friday as moisture moves north into the
   region. Some stronger storms could result in flash flooding, 
   damaging winds, and large hail.

 - The flood threat lingers for eastern areas this weekend before storm
   chances decrease early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1218 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

A large upper low will make "landfall" over southern California 
later tonight. To our southeast, an upper level ridge is spinning 
away leaving us sandwiched in between the two systems. Anomalously 
high moisture is being pushed into the area. Showers and 
thunderstorms will pop up initially over the AZ/NM border during 
the middle afternoon today and looks to continue into later 
tonight before fizzling away. Thunderstorms have the potential to 
become strong to severe today where damaging wind gusts (58+ mph) 
and/or severe hail (1"+) is possible. A Marginal risk (Level 1/5) 
for severe thunderstorms is in effect today encompassing the area 
along and west of the Continental Divide. 

The upper low starts to lift out over SoCal and southern NV area 
Thursday afternoon. PW values will reach 1.1"-1.2" which would be in 
record breaking category. In addition, plenty of dynamics associated 
with this upper trough where 30-40kt of 0-6km shear expected 
Thursday afternoon. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms expected 
generally along and west of the Rio Grande. A Marginal Risk is in 
effect for the Rio Grande and west. A small area of a Slight Risk 
(Level 2/5) in portions of the Gila region tomorrow. Damaging wind 
gusts, severe hail, and even a small risk for a tornado or two 
possible Thursday afternoon generally along and west of the 
Continental Divide. A Flood Watch has been issued for the Gila 
region Thursday starting at noon through 6 AM Friday morning. Models 
have been focusing over this region for heavy accumulations around 
2" or so. The anomalous moisture in the air will promote heavy 
rainfall in a short amount of time.

A piece of energy pinches off of the main upper trough Friday which 
will only continue the threat of flooding and severe weather. Drier 
air does look like it will have made it into far western portions of 
the area but elsewhere will have a good chance to see thunderstorms. 
PWs look to drop to around 1", which is still well above normal plus 
30-40kt of bulk shear. Flash flooding will continue to be a concern. 
Another Marginal risk for severe weather is in effect for the 
central portions of the CWA Friday.

Heading into Saturday, the second closed low will provide a source 
of lift for thunderstorms again focusing east of the Continental 
Divide. PWs do dip at this time to 0.8"-1" focusing out east, so 
flash flooding will still be a concern. Bulk shear will be around
35-50kt that afternoon allowing for another round of severe 
weather likely. The second low finally starts to lift out Sunday 
morning drying out much of the area from west to east. Some 
lingering storm chances Sunday for far eastern locations that 
afternoon. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 529 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Thunderstorms will continue to develop along the NM/AZ border and
will expand in coverage eastward over the NM Bootheel and Gila
Region. Lower confidence if any storms will reach KDMN and KTCS 
this evening but can not rule it out. Thunderstorms are not 
expected at KLRU or KELP this evening. 

Widespread thunderstorms will redevelop Thursday afternoon after 
18Z that will likely impact KTCS, KDMN and KLRU with mvfr
conditions due to reduced visibilities in heavy rain mixed with
hail between 18Z and 00Z. Storms will continue over those sites 
into the evening. Thunderstorms will impact KELP later Thursday 
evening after 00Z just beyond the current valid period for this 
TAF issuance period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 125 PM MDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Low fire weather concerns through the week ahead as min RHs stay 
above critical thresholds and 20 foot winds stay 5-10 mph each 
afternoon. Min RH values across the lowlands will be 30-50% each 
afternoon through early next week. Min RHs will be anywhere from 50-
80% in the area mountains each day. Continued rain chances each day. 

Focus for storms Thursday will be along and west of the Rio Grande. 
Mostly areawide chances Friday, but drier air does push into far 
western locations Saturday dampening chances out that way, but 
elsewhere will still have good chances. Lingering storm chances 
exist for far west TX and Otero Co Sunday. Each day through Saturday 
and potentially into Sunday will feature a risk for flash flooding, 
hail, and severe wind gusts in the strongest storms. 

&&
